clue.text: Getting out of such transport, people lost their heads

definitions.text: Getting out of such transport, people lost their heads

parts.words: Getting out of such transport, people lost their heads
parts.note: the cart that carried condemned prisoners to the guillotine in the French Revolution: those who stepped down from it were beheaded

explanation.surface: A grim remark about passengers who panicked on leaving some vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost their heads' reads as panicking; literally it means beheading, which points to the French Revolution's carts.
explanation.definitionFit: The cart taking victims to the guillotine is the classic vehicle whose riders were then beheaded.

clue.text: "X" with powerful following that can be maintained

indicators.note: the powerful word comes after the X word
the powerful word comes after the X word

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
able means capable, having power

explanation.surface: A powerful X sounds like a mathematical claim that holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X' looks like a letter or unknown; it is the Roman ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be defended or held.

clue.text: End on time — this may well be noticed

indicators.note: the letters 'End on time' may well be turned into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Finishing punctually will probably get you noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This may well be' signals that END ON TIME is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mentioned is referred to, remarked on, noticed.

clue.text: Splendid present, gold mounted

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the letters climb, so they read upwards

parts.note: to lay a case before someone is to present it
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gold-mounted gift is magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' reads as set in gold; in a down clue it turns LAY OR upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal can mean magnificent, fit for a king.

clue.text: A person who keeps reading

parts.note: reads as an avid reader, but the person keeps, looks after, reading matter

explanation.surface: A description of a bookworm who never stops reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps reading' suggests reading constantly; it means keeping books.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper of a book collection in an institution.

clue.text: Not all will be pleased a testy fellow calms down

indicators.note: only part of the run 'pleased a testy' is used, so the letters sit inside those words
only part of the run 'pleased a testy' is used, so the letters sit inside those words

explanation.surface: A grumpy man is calmed, though not everyone is happy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm someone down, especially with a drug, is to tranquillise them.

clue.text: A change of underwear

definitions.meaning: a woman's simple undergarment, a chemise

explanation.surface: Fresh underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A change of underwear' reads as clean clothes; it is two senses joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a move or alteration and a plain chemise worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Advocating closing after getting fed-up

indicators.note: the closing word comes after the turned word
in a down clue, up turns the letters to read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
an ending is a closing

explanation.surface: Someone argues for shutting down after becoming fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed-up' looks like annoyed; 'up' turns FED to DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Defending a cause is speaking in support of it, as an advocate does.

clue.text: "Dynasty" in China retaining Western nasal sound

indicators.note: the dynasty word holds the western letter inside

parts.note: the Tang (T'ang) was a Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: A Chinese dynasty keeps a Western accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynasty' is in quotes to suggest a TV show; it is the Tang dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of voice.

clue.text: Put away in case it gives rise 'to anger in some woman

indicators.note: the anger word sits inside the word for some woman

parts.note: she refers to any woman
heat is anger, passion

explanation.surface: Put it away safely, because it provokes some woman's rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away in case' is the definition, a sword returned to its scabbard; 'it gives rise to' is only a link, so 'anger' must be read as the noun heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade into its scabbard.

clue.text: A simpleton's lodging in New York

indicators.note: the lodging word is set inside the letters for New York

parts.note: an inn is a place offering lodging

explanation.surface: A fool is staying somewhere in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodging' looks like a verb describing where the simpleton lives; it is a noun, the place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly, foolish person is a simpleton.

clue.text: Paper carrier for crisp suit

parts.note: crisp speech is short and to the point, i.e. brief
a lawsuit is a legal case

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a bag for carrying documents to go with a smart suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crisp suit' looks like sharp tailoring; 'suit' is a lawsuit, a CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat case for carrying documents and papers.

clue.text: Shining fish ending in a tin, perhaps

parts.note: brill is a flatfish related to turbot, here ending in, i.e. followed at the end by, the next piece

indicators.note: the letters of 'a tin' are given only as a possible arrangement, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A gleaming fish that may end up in a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending in a tin' looks like the fish's fate; 'ending in' only places the reshuffled 'a tin' (IANT) at the end, with 'perhaps' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shining is bright and dazzling.

clue.text: "Frighted the reign of Chaos and old ______" Milton

definitions.text: "Frighted the reign of Chaos and old ______" Milton

parts.words: "Frighted the reign of Chaos and old ______" Milton
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Paradise Lost Book I, where the fallen angels' shout scares Chaos and its dark partner

explanation.surface: A line of Milton with its last word left blank for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped 'old' and the blank; the page prints the full quotation, Paradise Lost I.543.
explanation.definitionFit: In Milton's cosmos the primeval darkness is personified alongside Chaos, completing the quoted line.

clue.text: Eastern service that is for the bondsman

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services
ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A remark that some eastern service is meant for a bonded labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bondsman' is the British machine that picks Premium Bond prize numbers; 'service' is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium Bond winners in Britain are chosen by a random-number computer, the bonds' selector.

clue.text: A dance group might see nothing amiss

indicators.note: amiss means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dance troupe might see nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amiss' rearranges MIGHT SEE plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish reel for eight dancers, or any group of eight.

clue.text: Start testing A1 components

indicators.note: the letters are treated as parts to be reassembled in a new order

parts.note: A1 is read as the letters A and I, the figure 1 standing for the letter I

explanation.surface: Begin checking top-quality parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Components' looks like the things tested; it signals that TESTING and AI (A1) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it going or provoke it.

clue.text: Rush — a spring flowering plant

parts.note: speed means rush
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Hurry: a spring plant is flowering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, a small blue-flowered plant.

clue.text: An expert in woman's make-up?

parts.note: suggests a cosmetics expert, but make-up means bodily structure, of (wo)man

explanation.surface: A beautician skilled in cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' reads as cosmetics; it means how the body is built.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies the structure of the body.

clue.text: Lack of mice in the church?

definitions.text: Lack of mice in the church?

parts.words: Lack of mice in the church?
parts.note: alludes to 'poor as a church mouse': what church mice suffer from is poverty

explanation.surface: A question about why a church has no mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lack of mice' reads as an absence of mice; it is the lack, i.e. the want, that the mice have.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe poverty, the condition of the proverbial church mouse.

clue.text: One who doesn't feel obliged to discover where the fire is

definitions.meaning: split as '...', where a fire burns

explanation.surface: Someone who owes no thanks goes looking for a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person; and a hearth fire sits in the grate.

clue.text: A note to file — "Hold on'

parts.note: G is a musical note
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: A memo to put away in a file says to wait a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold on' looks like 'wait'; it means hold on to, grip.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip or seize firmly.

clue.text: Head's quiet retreat

parts.note: p (piano) means quiet in music
recede means retreat

explanation.surface: The headmaster's peaceful retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To go before, or lead.

clue.text: Great get-together of soldier and social worker

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
an ant is a social insect, a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A big meeting between a soldier and a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge or enormous in size.

clue.text: Like bed? Then this is the place!

parts.note: as means like
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A question about beds answered with a destination.
explanation.walkthrough: The place is the English racecourse at Ascot, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot, the Berkshire racecourse, is a well-known venue.

clue.text: Rare continental articles used up

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
der is German for 'the'
done means finished or used up

explanation.surface: Uncommon European articles that have been worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' looks like 'uncommon'; it is the steak sense, lightly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is lightly cooked, not cooked through.

clue.text: Superior — philosopher given employment

parts.note: U means upper-class
a sage is a wise thinker

explanation.surface: A superior thinker is given work.
explanation.walkthrough: U = upper-class, from 'U and non-U' British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is used.

clue.text: Broadcast concerning the non-professional

parts.note: re means about, concerning
lay means non-professional, not of the clergy or a profession

explanation.surface: A broadcast about amateurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' is both noun and verb; relay as verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to pass on or transmit.

clue.text: A charge on sports in Alaska

indicators.note: sports as a verb means plays around with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fee for sporting activities somewhere in Alaska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sports' looks like a noun; as a verb it rearranges CHARGE ON to NCHORAGE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in the US state is the place in question.

clue.text: One -having some knowledge about running water

indicators.note: the knowledge word goes about, around, the one
the knowledge word goes about, around, the one

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone with a little knowledge about flowing water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running water' is a river, the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: France's longest river is a body of running water.

clue.text: Intense fanatic

definitions.meaning: holding views far beyond the moderate

explanation.surface: Two words for a zealot's fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both utmost in degree and radical in opinion.

clue.text: Still to be seen in recent clothing for a youngster

indicators.note: the still word appears inside the recent word

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in 'the late news'
yet means still

explanation.surface: Something motionless visible in modern children's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adjective; it is the adverb YET.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of clothes and linen for a newborn baby.
